channel.title: Finality
channel.description: Finality reports crypto news: protocol upgrades, network incidents, exchange and stablecoin developments, regulation and the projects shaping blockchain.

item.title: Cancel a Partially Filled Limit Order Without Losing Track
item.description: A partial fill changes how much of your order remains executable. Check the settled amount, cancel the remainder, and verify the final state before replacing it.

item.title: How zerofi bridges Monero, and why Bitcoin is not supported
item.description: ZeroFi currently wraps Monero into zXMR on Ethereum Sepolia through bonded-node custody; Bitcoin is not supported, and the route remains a testnet flow.

item.title: Horizen EON Bridge After Shutdown: What Still Works
item.description: Horizen EON stopped at a migration snapshot: eligible EOA ZEN moved to Base, while contract balances, wZEN and DeFi positions stayed outside the transfer.

item.title: Interactive Brokers Opens Ethereum Staking to Eligible Clients
item.description: Interactive Brokers has opened Ethereum staking to eligible clients through zerohash, with rewards set by network rules and unstaking subject to delays.

item.title: Solana Activates Alpenglow, Targeting 150ms Finality
item.description: Solana validators replaced TowerBFT with Alpenglow at slot 459,653,000, shifting votes into certificates and targeting finality in about 150 milliseconds.

item.title: Rango Bridge: what an integration adds to cross-chain swaps
item.description: Rango Bridge can add cross-chain route discovery and execution, but its value depends on whether your app can handle multi-step signing, fees and status tracking.

item.title: Choosing a super bridge route: fees, finality and asset form
item.description: Cross-chain routes trade settlement time, asset form and trust assumptions against cost; compare each route’s steps and destination outcome before signing.

item.title: Blockchain.com launches crypto options as it seeks US licenses
item.description: Blockchain.com has launched short-dated crypto options in supported markets, while seeking CFTC registrations that could enable regulated derivatives trading in the US.

item.title: Five Checks for Baibai Quotes and Base Swap Routes
item.description: Compare a Baibai quote with a Base aggregator route by checking execution, fees, slippage and token flow; the displayed output alone cannot prove the route.

item.title: How ERC-2612 Permits Can Bundle a Bridge Deposit
item.description: An ERC-2612 permit lets a supported bridge set token allowance from a signature and pull funds in one transaction, but the bridge must handle the permit correctly.

item.title: JPMorgan Brings JPM Coin to Ethereum for Institutions
item.description: JPMorgan has deployed its dollar deposit token on Ethereum for institutional clients, adding a public-chain venue for onchain payments and tokenized-asset settlement.

item.title: JPMorgan extends JPMD transfers to Ethereum
item.description: J.P. Morgan is extending JPMD to Ethereum, adding the network to the institutional transfer options already available on Base and widening its onchain reach.

item.title: Ledger reviews wallet sales after CryptoBilis-linked theft
item.description: Ledger is reviewing reseller controls after an implanted hardware component in wallets sold through CryptoBilis was linked to about $90 million in crypto theft.

item.title: Estimate Bridge Fee Tiers From Net Proceeds
item.description: Compare bridge quotes by what arrives after fees, then check route limits, token decimals and separate transaction costs before sending funds across chains.

item.title: How to Move Treasury Tokens for a Chain Incentive
item.description: Moving treasury tokens for a chain incentive means matching the approved allocation to the destination contract, transfer path and final on-chain state.

item.title: Vault Liquidity and Order Books Price Trades Differently
item.description: Pool swaps price against shared inventory, while order books match bids and asks; the better route depends on depth, execution control, fees and timing.

item.title: Which Fees Remain After You Cancel a Bridge Route?
item.description: Canceling a bridge route does not undo transactions already included on-chain: you may still pay for approval, source-chain gas and any completed bridge work.

item.title: A Stablecoin Funding Cutoff Is a Payment Deadline, Not a Network Rule
item.description: A funding cutoff is a provider’s processing deadline, not a stablecoin network shutdown; learn which rail, time zone and confirmation rule controls availability.

item.title: Swap Into the Fee Token a Cross-Chain Message Requires
item.description: A cross-chain message fee is paid in the token required by its source contract path; swap before sending, retain gas, and verify the live quote and accepted fee asset.

item.title: Cross-Chain Swap Stuck? Check Its State Before Retrying
item.description: A pending swap is a state problem, not a signal to submit again: verify the source transaction, route status and destination claim or refund path first.
